title: Roberto Acciaiuoli to the Signoria from Amiens, 23 October 1513: Bourbon to Burgundy, the king's anger and the English embarkation (catalogue 2351)

steps.what: Codex applies Dudout's pandolfini1514 key v6 to a first transcription and reads the Bourbon passage.
Claude re-transcribes both faces from enlarged line strips with the key in hand; two fresh instances make blind passes from shape names alone.
Doc. 190 aligned sign by sign against its clear copy 191; corrections fitted on nine lines, 84-94% agreement on 93 held-out signs whose clear word was read before decoding.
Reading with v6 plus the 190/191 values: 85% of signs. A sign count including bracketed corrections was first reported as 96% of words, which overstated it.

Second blind round on the thirteen hardest lines from tighter crops; signs both readers agree on are adopted. Opens V8-10 and clauses at V1, V5, R6, R12. The number 26 read at R12 is withdrawn, then restored with a query after review.
Gabbrielli's key no. 120 for Acciaioli found on DECODE (R5807) and transcribed: confirms the values and 22 = Lanzichinecchi, corrects se to quando, adds quanto, ora, tanto, galee.

Codex reviews the reading against the manuscript and key images: strict word count 86-90%, not 96%; corrects nientedimeno, perché, facto, passaggio; asks for queries on supplied words. Applied where confirmed on crops; status set to read in part.
Gabbrielli's keys no. 89 and no. 111 for Acciaioli checked for the numbers 15, 26, 47: both are different ciphers.

After Dan Bourdeau's review: every departure from the key marked in the reading and counted as a hole; figures written as numerals; two blind surveys of the 67 places of the sign 2 by fresh Claude instances (sign2_forms.tsv). The squat form goes with b at 12 of the 14 places read b but also stands at 4 of the 53 read c, over the bar set beforehand, so no sign is renamed.

Write-up escalation (AI agent, for the maintainers): Dudout's key v6 compared with key.tsv by sign name on this letter (same value at 1,690 of 1,887 signs, another at 31, none at 166) and the nomenclators of pandolfini1514 and pandolfini1515 searched for 15, 26 and 47. v6 has 26 = Arciduca, which fits the king's words at R12 (sendo io loro soprano signore); 47 is in neither key; 15 occurs once in pandolfini1515, unvalued, beside the Swiss. Proposals only: the reading and the count are unchanged.

The F sign with a raised mark (R13, V05) compared on crops with doc. 190 verso line 3, where an F with a raised circle faces essere in the clear copy 191. Essere reads at both places, but Gabbrielli's key gives effetto for F with a raised 0 and the mark is not told apart at 1272 px. Left open. corsi1513, of the same weeks, is in another key and gives nothing.

The word struck out under Rubertet on the clear copy doc. 191 (line 16), where the cipher of doc. 190 has 15, enlarged to see whether the clerk first wrote the value of 15: it begins with what looks like a v and is about nine letters long; not readable at 1272 px.
OCR text of Desjardins and Canestrini vol. II (archive.org) searched again for the letter: Amiens 26 Sept 1513 (pp. 588-589), then Malines 20 Nov 1513; no letter of 23 Oct 1513.

Key replay tried with docs/_replay.py (raw key on the transcription against reading-it.md): 653 of 752 words of the reading are the key's output, 64 differ with a mark, 24 unread. The 11 places it flagged as unmarked were each traced in the alignment to an unread group whose mark covers several signs, the number 15, or a supplied letter that repeats its neighbour (pare [bene], via [a]); no unmarked change of the reading was found. The adapter is not kept, since the tool cannot settle those ties.

outcome.method_basis: Gabbrielli's nineteenth-century reconstruction of Acciaioli's cipher (no. 120), made from other letters, gives the text: by the source column of key.tsv, 1,774 of the 1,887 signs take a Gabbrielli value. No plaintext of this letter was used. The system was first recognised from Dudout's pandolfini1514 key, and the cipher letter 190 with its clear copy 191 of the same day added or corrected a few values (the beta-like e, the word signs vostra and nostro); values resting on this letter alone are marked 192 in key.tsv.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading-it.md, cipher words under ## Reading: 660 of 757 are the key's output with nothing supplied or changed. The 97 holes are 41 words with a bracketed letter or second key value (among them the 20 departures of 192-repairs.tsv), 26 proposed words marked [?word], 25 unread words and 5 numbers with no value. Elided forms count as one word; the clear closing is not counted.
outcome.notes: Key state partial: of the eight numbers used as code words in this letter (2, 4, 6, 15, 20, 22, 26, 47), 15, 26 and 47 have no value in Gabbrielli's key, and two word signs (B with a raised 1, F with a raised mark) are open. Proposals from the write-up escalation of 24 Nov 2026 (26 = Arciduca from Dudout's key, essere for the F sign) are not counted as read. Same cipher as pandolfini1514 as far as the two key files compare; kept as its own target because its values come from Gabbrielli's key for Acciaioli. No image is reproduced.

texts.summary: Louis XII has ordered Bourbon into Burgundy with lances and Landsknechte; news of a rout has overturned a plan; the king is angry at people who yielded to the English; the English king has shipped his baggage and his army is embarking, part of it at Calais; the king says he is secure and will fight if the Swiss move; the prelates leave for Rome after All Saints.
texts.note: 192-literal.txt is the unedited output of key.tsv. The reading departs from it at the 20 places of 192-repairs.tsv and wherever it prints brackets; every departure is marked and counted as a hole. read_share counts words read with nothing supplied or changed (660 of 757).

reading_review.by: OpenAI Codex, integration review of PR #841 for the maintainers (AI reviewer)
reading_review.note: Read the continuous Italian against the English. The dispatch is coherent but raw, with proposed words, marked repairs and unresolved groups. Replayed the raw key on all 41 lines and removed one duplicated R01 in the filed output. Reviewed the 20-row repair list and the failed sign-2 separation. The contributor reports 660/757 sure; a separate markup-based tally gave 659/759, also read in part. The earlier maintainer review checked three manuscript passages; this pass compared committed texts and did not recheck the images.
